data.title: UCP Returns Logic Hijacking — Void Return and Verify Step Bypass
data.description: Detects exploitation of the UCP returns state machine where AI agents skip the order.return.verify step and trigger settlement.refund.instant() using fraudulent tracking IDs (e.g., void-000). Threat actors embed hidden instructions in product page HTML metadata or invisible span tags that are ingested by the agent when it reads return instructions. The agent then processes the malicious command as a high-priority system update, bypassing return verification and issuing refunds without valid shipping confirmation. At scale, organized crime groups deploy bot farms to initiate thousands of void returns per hour, potentially liquidating a retailer's cash reserves. This rule targets Phase 4 (Execution) by detecting refund primitives triggered without proper verification, void tracking IDs, and anomalous refund velocity.

detection.condition: selection_void_tracking or selection_verify_skip or (selection_no_shipping_scan and aggregation_velocity)

enrichment_required.source: Shipping carrier enrichment (validate tracking ID against carrier API for actual shipment confirmation)
UCP state machine enrichment (verify order.return.verify step completion status)

falsepositives: Merchant-initiated refunds that bypass standard return flow (e.g., customer service overrides)
Digital product returns where physical shipping verification is not applicable
